title: Surgical Resection for Multiple Hepatocellular Carcinomas Following Atezolizumab Plus Bevacizumab Therapy: A Case Report
content: Unresectable multifocal hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is generally managed with systemic therapy, including immune checkpoint inhibitors and molecular targeted agents. When adequate tumor control is achieved, conversion to surgical resection may become feasible. A 59-year-old man with untreated chronic hepatitis C was found to have seven HCC lesions during magnetic resonance imaging surveillance. Systemic therapy with atezolizumab (1200 mg/body) plus bevacizumab (15 mg/kg) was initiated for unresectable multifocal HCC. After three cycles, contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed tumor shrinkage, with a 28% reduction in the sum of target lesion diameters, corresponding to stable disease according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1. The future liver remnant volume was 39.2%. After two additional cycles of atezolizumab monotherapy as bridging therapy, the patient underwent extended right hepatectomy, including resection of segment 4 and partial resection of segment 2. Pathological examination confirmed R0 resection, with viable tumor cells and focal necrosis. The postoperative course was uneventful, and antiviral therapy for hepatitis C resulted in a sustained virological response. The patient remains recurrence-free. Systemic therapy with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab enabled successful conversion surgery for seven HCC lesions. This multimodal approach may represent a viable treatment option for carefully selected patients with initially unresectable multifocal HCC.
